clue.text: Cut joints for consumption in fast food restaurant

indicators.note: the cut word swallows the joints, as food is taken in for consumption

parts.note: to chop is to cut
hips are joints of the body

explanation.surface: A butcher slices up joints to be eaten at a takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for consumption' is the container signal: the joints are eaten, taken inside. A chip shop is a British takeaway selling fish and chips.
explanation.definitionFit: A chip shop is a British takeaway, a kind of fast food outlet selling fried fish and chips.

clue.text: Man has variety of briar added to a set of plant collections

parts.note: he stands for a man, the male pronoun

indicators.note: a variety of something is a different form of it, so the letters of briar are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man owns several kinds of briar, added to a range of plant collections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' is the anagram signal. 'Man has' tempts the name Herb, but that leaves too few letters for the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbaria are collections of dried plant specimens, the plural of herbarium, so a set of them.

clue.text: Pressure to take measure against bankrupt town

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics
an em is a printer's measure of width
broke means penniless, bankrupt

explanation.surface: Financial pressure leads to measures against a town gone bankrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: EM is a printer's unit of width. Pembroke is a town in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Pembroke is a historic town in south-west Wales, an example of a town.

clue.text: Sign of hospital having trouble in wintry weather

parts.note: H is the letter on road signs pointing to a hospital
to ail is to be troubled or unwell

explanation.surface: The hospital sign is in trouble during a spell of wintry weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Hail, frozen pellets falling from the sky, is a typical kind of wintry weather.

clue.text: Analyses villain in Dickens, from what we hear

indicators.note: signals that the villain's name is spoken and a word of the same sound is written

parts.note: Bill Sikes is the brutal villain of Dickens's novel Oliver Twist

explanation.surface: Someone studies a Dickens villain, going by hearsay.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Sikes is the murderous burglar in Oliver Twist; his surname is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To psych someone is informal for psychoanalysing them, so psyches means analyses.

clue.text: I falter, say, translating Perrault's works

indicators.note: translating turns text into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles while putting a French author's stories into English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translating' rearranges the ten letters of I FALTER SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Perrault wrote Cinderella and Sleeping Beauty, the classic stories of magic, so his works are of this kind.

clue.text: Dowdy swimmer keeps bottom covered

indicators.note: the swimmer holds the next word inside it
the bottom is wrapped by the swimmer, so it ends up covered

parts.note: a fish is a creature that swims
the rump is the backside, the bottom

explanation.surface: A frumpy bather wears a costume that keeps her rear decently covered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' and 'covered' together signal the container; the swimmer is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Frumpish means unfashionable and drab in dress, a close synonym of dowdy.

clue.text: House close to pretty French ski resort

parts.note: a chamber is a house of a parliament

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A house near a pretty resort in the French Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' takes the last letter of PRETTY. CHAMBER is a parliamentary house, as in the upper chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambery is a town in the French Alps of Savoie, a gateway to the ski slopes, so loosely a ski resort.

clue.text: Trawl netting most of favourite type of fish

indicators.note: the search word catches the next piece inside it, as a net does

parts.note: to trawl through something is to search it

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A fisherman trawls with nets, hoping for his favourite catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trawl' looks like fishing but means search; 'netting' is the container signal, and 'most of' drops the favourite's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea perch is a name for various marine fish such as the bass, so it is a type of fish.

clue.text: Split up with my girl in bad-tempered way

indicators.note: split means broken apart, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone splits up with his girlfriend in a foul mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' rearranges UP and MY GIRL; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumpily means in a surly, irritable manner, which is acting bad-temperedly.

clue.text: Maybe Queen Mother kept a type of plant

indicators.note: the card and mother hold the next letter between them

parts.note: a queen is one example of a playing card
mom is the American word for mother
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Queen Mother may have kept a particular plant in her garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen Mother' looks like one royal person, but the words split: queen is a playing card and Mother is MOM. 'kept' puts A between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardamom is an aromatic plant of the ginger family, whose seeds are used as a spice.

clue.text: Preliminary printing hope for set to be corrected

indicators.note: text to be corrected has its errors put right, so its letters will be rearranged

explanation.surface: A trial print raises hope that the type will be corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be corrected' rearranges the ten letters of HOPE FOR SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A proof sheet is a trial print run off before final printing so that errors can be checked.

clue.text: Beer ends up being discovered in school, and there's talk of flogging

indicators.note: these pieces are found inside the school abbreviation

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upward, so backwards

parts.note: tips are ends, as in fingertips

explanation.surface: Boys caught drinking beer at school face talk of a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the ends in this down clue, and 'being discovered in' places beer and the turned ends inside the school abbreviation. 'flogging' is British slang for selling, not beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Flogging is British slang for selling, so a sales pitch is the talk a seller gives.

clue.text: Skimmed cream, low in calories

indicators.note: skimming takes off the top, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: the cream of a group is its elite, the best

explanation.surface: Skimmed cream is advertised as a low-calorie product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skimmed' removes the top letter of ELITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lite is a marketing spelling of light used for food and drink with reduced calories.

clue.text: Female duo showing a bit of leg

parts.note: Pat is a woman's name, the first of the pair
Ella is a woman's name, the second of the pair

explanation.surface: Two women flash a little leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duo' asks for two female names placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the kneecap, a bone forming part of the leg.

clue.text: Soft cushion all but swallowed by a new pet dog

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft

indicators.note: the shortened cushion goes down inside the pair of letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: all but the last letter is used

parts.note: a pillow is a cushion

explanation.surface: A new pet dog has all but swallowed a soft cushion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but' drops the cushion's last letter, and 'swallowed by' puts what remains between A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: The papillon is a small toy spaniel kept as a pet, named for its butterfly-shaped ears.

clue.text: Authorities raised prize money

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word turns it upward, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a pot is a prize, as in a trophy cup or winnings
brass is British slang for money

explanation.surface: The authorities put up the prize money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns POT upward. Brass is northern British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The top brass are the people in highest authority in an organisation, originally senior officers.

clue.text: Disease-ridden country?

parts.note: read as an adjective, a land infected with blight, a plant disease; really an affectionate soldiers' name for Britain

explanation.walkthrough: Blighty is old British slang, from the World Wars, for Britain as home; the clue pretends it means full of blight.
explanation.definitionFit: Blighty is a fond slang name for Britain or England, used especially by soldiers serving abroad.

clue.text: Mild oath concerning restless type

parts.note: gad is an old euphemism for God, a mild oath
about means concerning, on the subject of

explanation.surface: Someone mildly curses about a fidgety person.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadabout is someone who restlessly goes from place to place seeking amusement.

clue.text: Mostly keep map inside aircraft

indicators.note: the map goes inside the shortened keep
most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle
a plan is a map or drawing

explanation.surface: Keep the map tucked away inside the aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep' is the castle tower, not the verb; 'Mostly' drops its last letter and 'inside' sets the map within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A towplane is an aircraft that tows gliders into the air.

clue.text: Given heavy blow, son's carried with great difficulty

parts.note: to lug something is to carry it with great effort

explanation.surface: After a heavy blow, the son had to be carried with great effort.
explanation.definitionFit: To be slugged is to be struck hard, especially with the fist, so given a heavy blow.

clue.text: Pop publicists

parts.note: a PA is a press agent, one publicist
a second PA, a second press agent, makes the plural

explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'publicists' gives two press agents, PA and PA.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop and papa are both familiar words for father.

clue.text: For NASA it's a drop in the ocean

definitions.text: For NASA it's a drop in the ocean

parts.words: For NASA it's a drop in the ocean
parts.note: the idiom for something tiny is read literally, as a space capsule dropping into the sea on its return

explanation.walkthrough: A drop in the ocean usually means a trivial amount; here it is literal, as Apollo capsules came down in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A splashdown is a spacecraft's landing in the sea, as NASA capsules returned to Earth.

clue.text: Out of control, urchin goes staggering unsteadily

indicators.note: the answer comes out of these words, its letters lifted from them in sequence

explanation.surface: A wild urchin staggers about, out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of' pulls the answer from contrOL URCHIN Goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurching means moving with sudden unsteady rolling movements, as when staggering.

clue.text: Baked dish left to cool outside

indicators.note: the word for cool goes around the letter for left

parts.note: to fan something is to cool it

explanation.surface: A baked dish is left outside to cool down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts FAN around L.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open pastry case with a sweet or savoury baked filling.

clue.text: Proceed with route touring everything — one belted

indicators.note: going around something, so the first pieces surround the next

parts.note: to go is to proceed
all means everything
a way is a route

explanation.surface: Proceed along a route that tours everything, with seatbelt fastened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts everything inside the first piece. The Belted Galloway is a Scottish cattle breed with a white band round its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Belted Galloway is a Scottish beef cattle breed with a white belt, so a Galloway can be one belted.

clue.text: Old boy's story about Conservative in bar

parts.note: OB is an old boy, a former pupil, with the S kept

indicators.note: the story goes around the letter for Conservative

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A former pupil tells a story about a Tory in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts C inside TALE. 'bar' looks like a pub but means a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar is something that blocks the way, a barrier or obstacle.

clue.text: Get coloured curtains, we're told, for kitchen areas

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is said and a word of the same sound is written

parts.note: to dye nets is to get net curtains coloured

explanation.surface: Advice to have the curtains dyed for the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: DYE NETS, said aloud, gives the answer; nets are net curtains.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinettes are small dining areas, often part of or next to a kitchen.
